1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Wear ANSI Z87.1 impact safety glasses whenever cutting, drilling, or testing moving mechanisms.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. SENSE (Perception & Telemetry): Ultrasonic time-of-flight, LIDAR, optical wheel encoders, IMU gyroscopes, and limit switches measure world state.
2. PLAN (Microcontroller Decision Logic): State machines and PID feedback controllers compute error (Target minus Measured) 50 to 1,000 times per second.
3. ACT (Mechanical Power Conversion): DC gearmotors, hobby servos, stepper motors, and pneumatic cylinders convert electrical signals into motion.
4. FEEDBACK (Closed-Loop Correction): Encoders verify actual wheel/arm travel and automatically compensate for battery voltage drop or ramp slope.
1.worked_field_example: Before testing a high-torque spinning arm, verify the red E-Stop button cuts main battery power within 0.1 seconds.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: Run a four-point pre-power safety inspection covering ANSI Z87.1 eyewear, E-Stop continuity, LiPo safe bag, and pinch-point guards.
1.real_world_connection_box: OSHA, ANSI Z87.1 & FIRST Robotics Safety Standard: Wear ANSI Z87.1 impact safety glasses whenever cutting, drilling, or testing moving mechanisms. Charge lithium-polymer batteries inside a fire-resistant LiPo bag and wire a physical Emergency Stop switch in series with motor power.

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: An autonomous robot executes a closed feedback loop where sensors measure the environment, the controller plans, and actuators move.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1:1 Direct Drive (12T -> 12T): Output speed equals motor RPM and output torque equals motor stall torque; zero mechanical advantage.
1:3 Geared Up for Speed (36T -> 12T): Triples output shaft RPM while cutting available torque to one-third; stalls easily on steep ramps.
3:1 Geared Down for Torque (12T -> 36T): Multiplies lifting and climbing torque 3x (minus ~5% friction) at one-third speed for heavy robot arms.
6 Degrees of Freedom (3 Linear + 3 Rotary): Full 3D workspace requires Surge (X), Sway (Y), Heave (Z) plus Roll, Pitch, and Yaw wrist orientation.
2.worked_field_example: An ultrasonic sensor detects an obstacle at 15 cm (Sense), the microcontroller computes a 90-degree turn (Plan), and wheel motors pivot (Act).
2.counselor_tabletop_demo: Trace a single obstacle-avoidance cycle across the ultrasonic rangefinder, microcontroller board, and DC gearmotors on the robot cutaway.
2.real_world_connection_box: NASA Robotics Alliance Sense-Plan-Act Standard: An autonomous robot executes a closed feedback loop where sensors measure the environment, the controller plans, and actuators move.

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Gear ratio equals driven teeth divided by driver teeth, trading rotational speed directly for proportional output torque.
core_mechanism_bullets: Stage 1: Problem Constraints & Sketches: Define task geometry, weight/size limits, and sketch at least two competing drivetrain/manipulator concepts.
Stage 2: Subsystem Prototype & Wiring: Build modular chassis and actuator assembly with color-coded wiring (Red V+, Black GND, Yellow/White Signal).
Stage 3: State-Machine Code & Sensor Test: Write clean modular functions with serial telemetry printouts to verify raw sensor thresholds before full speed.
Stage 4: Five-Trial Quantitative Validation: Run 5 consecutive repeatability trials, record cycle times and failure modes, and document design refinements.
4.worked_field_example: Driving a 36-tooth spur gear with a 12-tooth motor pinion yields a 3-to-1 reduction that triples lifting torque at one-third speed.
4.counselor_tabletop_demo: Mesh a small driver gear with a large driven gear to count how many driver rotations produce one full rotation of the output shaft.
4.real_world_connection_box: ASME & FIRST Mechanical Transmission Standard: Gear ratio equals driven teeth divided by driver teeth, trading rotational speed directly for proportional output torque.
